To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
salmon farming can increase sea lice infestation of juvenile salmon by four orders of magnitude.

the transmission dynamics of sea ice from a salmon farm were four orders of magnitude above ambient levels and that the farm-induced sea lice infestation extended 30 km down two wild salmon migration routes.
the farm produced an infection pressure of sea lice that was four orders of magnitudes greater than ambient levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transmission dynamics of parasites from farm salmon to wild salmon, and how these dynamics may be affected by salmon farming.
the transmission dynamics of parasites from farmed to wild hosts.
the transmission dynamics of sea ice from farm to wild juvenile salmon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single salmon farm can increase the transmission dynamics of sea-louse infestations to wild juvenile salmon to a level that can be detrimental to their survival.
a single salmon farm can alter the transmission dynamics of sea ice to juvenile salmon for at least 75 km along their migration routes.

a single salmon farm in a narrow fjord can alter the natural transmission dynamics and infection pressures of parasitic sea-louse infestations on juvenile wild Pacific salmon for up to 75 km downstream of the farm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
salmon farms are a source of parasitic sea-lice that can be transported by currents to wild juvenile salmon.
the farm produced a cohort of lice that was four orders of magnitudes greater than ambient levels that infected wild salmonids for a distance of 75 km along the migration routes.

salmon farms can be a source of parasitic sea-lice to wild juvenile salmonids, that the sea-lice can be transmitted from the salmon farm to the wild salmonids, that sea-lice can reproduce on wild juvenile salmonids and that the sea-liche reproduction can amplify the infection pressure to the wild salmon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salmon farms can have a dramatic effect on the transmission of sea lice from farms to the wild and that the effect is not restricted to the farm vicinity.
a single salmon farm can have a dramatic impact on the natural sea lice dynamics of wild salmon, and the impact of salmon farms on wild salmonids is probably much greater than previously recognized.
the impact of salmon farms on wild salmonids can be measured in terms of infection pressure and can be quantified in the field.
